source: Toprank Review Academy (TRA) Nursing Module – Complete Handout

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: Which position is used for a mother with endometritis?
questions.rationale: Semi-Fowler's promotes drainage of lochia; antibiotics are given.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Endometritis (PDF p. 213)

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: Calf pain on dorsiflexion of the foot postpartum suggests:
questions.rationale: A positive Homans' sign suggests thrombophlebitis; heparin may be given.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Thrombophlebitis (PDF p. 213)

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: A newborn lifts only the head when prone; later the chest. Which principle is this?
questions.rationale: Development proceeds head to tail (cephalocaudal).
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Principles of G&D (PDF p. 214)
questions.quote: Development proceeds from their head to tail

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: A 3-year-old colors best with a large crayon; a 12-year-old writes with a fine pen. Which principle?
questions.rationale: Development proceeds from gross to refined skills.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Principles of G&D (PDF p. 214)
questions.quote: A 3-yr old colors best with a large crayon; a 12-yr old can write with a fine pen

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: Per Freud, the toddler is in which stage?
questions.rationale: Infant oral, toddler anal (toilet training), preschool phallic, school-age latent, adolescent genital.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Freud's Stages (PDF p. 215)
questions.quote: Toddler Anal stage Control of urination and defecation

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: Erikson's task for the preschooler is:
questions.rationale: Preschool: initiative vs guilt; toddler: autonomy; school-age: industry; infant: trust.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Erikson's Stages (PDF p. 215)

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: What is the main fear of a hospitalized toddler?
questions.rationale: Toddler fear: separation; preschool: mutilation; school-age: displacement from school; adolescent: from peers.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Toddler (PDF p. 216)

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: Which play type is typical of toddlers?
questions.rationale: Infants: solitary; toddlers: parallel; preschoolers: associative; school-age: competitive.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Toddler (PDF p. 216)

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: Which toy is BEST for a toddler?
questions.rationale: Toddlers enjoy push and pull toys; infants mobiles; school-age table games.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Toddler (PDF p. 216)

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the Well Child (Neonate to Adolescent)
questions.stem: Which sign shows a toddler is ready for toilet training?
questions.rationale: Readiness includes staying dry 2 hours, waking dry from naps, removing clothes, and recognizing the urge.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Toilet Training (PDF p. 216)
questions.quote: Child is able to stay dry for 2 hours

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the Well Child (Neonate to Adolescent)
questions.stem: How should a nurse handle a toddler's negativism?
questions.rationale: Offer choices and avoid closed-ended questions that invite 'no'.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Toddler (PDF p. 216)

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: By what age does a child usually have all 20 deciduous teeth?
questions.rationale: Children generally have all 20 primary teeth by 3 years.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Toddler (PDF p. 216)
questions.quote: Children generally have all 20 of their deciduous teeth by 3 years of age

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: A preschooler believes the moon follows her because it is alive. This is:
questions.rationale: Magical thinking attributes thought and feeling to animals and objects.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Preschool Period (PDF p. 216)
questions.quote: They perceive animals and even inanimate objects as being capable of thought and feeling

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: What is the greatest fear of a hospitalized preschooler?
questions.rationale: Preschoolers fear mutilation and castration; use dolls and bandages to reassure.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Preschool Period (PDF p. 216)

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: A school-age child sorts objects by color and size. Which Piaget stage?
questions.rationale: Concrete operations (7–12 years) include classification and reversibility.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, School-age Period (PDF p. 217)

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: An adolescent solves hypothetical problems. Which Piaget stage?
questions.rationale: Formal operations (12+) involve hypothetical and scientific reasoning.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Adolescence (PDF p. 217)
questions.quote: Can solve hypothetical problems with scientific reasoning

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the Well Child (Neonate to Adolescent)
questions.stem: A newborn is blue at the extremities, HR 110, grimaces, has some flexion, and a weak cry. What is the APGAR?
questions.rationale: Acrocyanosis 1, HR >100 = 2, grimace 1, some flexion 1, weak cry 1 = 6.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, APGAR (PDF p. 218)

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the Well Child (Neonate to Adolescent)
questions.stem: An APGAR of 2 means the newborn needs:
questions.rationale: 1–3 poor, needs resuscitation; 4–7 fair, observe and stimulate; 8–10 good.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, APGAR (PDF p. 218)

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the Well Child (Neonate to Adolescent)
questions.stem: Which finding suggests a PRETERM newborn?
questions.rationale: Preterm signs: abundant lanugo, thin skin, few sole creases, flat ears, flat areola.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Gestational Age (PDF p. 218)

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the Well Child (Neonate to Adolescent)
questions.stem: By what age does an infant usually TRIPLE birth weight?
questions.rationale: Birth weight doubles by 6 months and triples by 12 months.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Profile of a Newborn (PDF p. 218)

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the Well Child (Neonate to Adolescent)
questions.stem: How much weight loss is normal in the first days of life?
questions.rationale: Newborns lose 5–10% of birth weight as maternal fluid-retaining hormones wear off.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Profile of a Newborn (PDF p. 218)
questions.quote: a newborn loses 5% to 10% of birth weight

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the Well Child (Neonate to Adolescent)
questions.stem: What is a normal newborn head circumference?
questions.rationale: Head 33–35 cm, chest 31–33 cm; the head is the largest circumference.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Profile of a Newborn (PDF p. 218)

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the Well Child (Neonate to Adolescent)
questions.stem: A Moro reflex persisting beyond 6 months may indicate:
questions.rationale: Persistence of the Moro reflex beyond 6 months may indicate brain damage.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Neurologic Assessment (PDF p. 219)
questions.quote: A persistent response lasting more than 6 months may indicate the occurrence of brain damage

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the Well Child (Neonate to Adolescent)
questions.stem: Which newborn vital sign is normal?
questions.rationale: Newborn apical rate 120–160, respirations 30–60.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Vital Signs (PDF p. 219)

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the Well Child (Neonate to Adolescent)
questions.stem: Scalp swelling that crosses suture lines after prolonged labor is:
questions.rationale: Caput crosses sutures and resolves in about 3 days; cephalhematoma does not cross sutures.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Physical Assessment (PDF p. 219)
questions.quote: Swelling of scalp caused by prolonged labor crosses over suture line

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the Well Child (Neonate to Adolescent)
questions.stem: What helps newborns produce heat?
questions.rationale: Brown adipose tissue increases metabolism to produce heat; newborns cannot shiver effectively.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Vital Signs (PDF p. 219)
questions.quote: Newborns can conserve heat by constricting blood vessels and moving blood away from the skin.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: About how many words does a 3-year-old know?
questions.rationale: About 900 words at 3, 1500 at 4, 2100 at 5.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Language Development (PDF p. 215)
